IN GREEN’S PROBLEM 47
JENSEN KOHLMEYER AND LIAM KRUER
ABSTRACT. We give a counterexample to the exact-containment formulation in the comments to Green’s Prob-
lem 47. The set
𝐴 = { 2} ∪ { 𝑞2 : 𝑞 is prime and 𝑞 ≡ 1 (mod 8 )}
occupies at most ( 𝑝 + 1)/2 residue classes modulo every odd prime 𝑝, but | 𝐴 ∩ [0, 𝑋 ] | is not 𝑂 (

is a two-moment identity for quadratic images over finite fields. The counting argument uses divergence of a

single element 2 leaves a subset of the squares; thus this construction does not refute a formulation allowing
finitely many exceptional elements, including Green and Harper’s Conjecture 1.7.

The construction starts with selected prime squares and adds one nonsquare. At a prime where 2 is a quadratic
nonresidue, none of the selected primes is zero modulo that prime. The missing zero residue makes room for
the added element without violating ( 1.1). Nevertheless, replacing zero by 2 changes the first two moments
in a way that no quadratic image can have. Primes in suitable arithmetic progressions allow this finite-field
obstruction to be applied to every rational quadratic.
Green and Harper [ 2, Conjecture 1.7] allow all but finitely many elements to belong to a rational quadratic
image. Their counting alternative also concerns arbitrarily large cutoffs for each logarithmic exponent. Our
set already satisfies their structural alternative, because
𝐴 \ { 2} ⊆ { 𝑧2 : 𝑧 ∈ Z} . (1.4)
Theorem 1.1 therefore addresses the stated exact-containment implication, not the general inverse large sieve
problem. No claim of priority is made for the construction.
